properties.label: Request payload
properties.tooltip: Full request body for a custom model endpoint, using exactly one of dataframe_split, dataframe_records, inputs, or instances. Prefer dataframe_split, because dataframe_records does not guarantee column ordering. See Model Serving query API.

properties.label: SQL statement
properties.description: Warning: bind values as parameters below. Never concatenate process variables into this text. Maximum statement size 16 MiB.
properties.value: SELECT * FROM samples.nyctaxi.trips WHERE fare_amount > :min_fare LIMIT 10
properties.tooltip: Named markers such as :min_fare are supported. Positional question-mark markers are not supported by the Databricks SQL Statement Execution API.

properties.label: Statement parameters
properties.tooltip: List of name, value, and type entries, and the only injection-safe way to pass values into the statement. The name omits the leading colon, type defaults to STRING, and omitting value binds NULL. Complex types such as ARRAY, MAP, and STRUCT are not supported.

properties.label: Wait timeout
properties.description: Either 0s, or between 5s and 50s.
properties.tooltip: How long to wait inline for the statement to finish. 0s returns immediately. If the statement does not finish within the window, the response carries a non-terminal state and the result must be polled with the Get statement operation.

choices.name: CONTINUE - keep running, poll for the result
CANCEL - cancel the statement on timeout

properties.label: Disposition

choices.name: INLINE - rows in the response (max 25 MiB)

properties.tooltip: How results are returned. INLINE embeds rows in the response and is capped at 25 MiB, and exceeding the cap aborts the statement without a result set. EXTERNAL_LINKS returns presigned URLs that expire after 15 minutes and must be fetched without an Authorization header.

properties.label: Statement ID
properties.tooltip: The statement_id returned by the Execute statement operation. Statements are removed roughly 12 hours after reaching a terminal state, after which these calls return HTTP 404.

properties.label: Chunk index

pattern.message: Must be a non-negative integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Zero-based chunk index, taken from next_chunk_index in a previous response. Use this to page through a result set larger than one chunk.

properties.label: Warehouse ID
properties.tooltip: Start and stop return immediately. Poll Get warehouse until state is RUNNING or STOPPED before relying on the change.

properties.label: Job ID

pattern.message: Must be a non-negative integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Numeric ID of the Databricks job to trigger.

properties.label: Job parameters
properties.tooltip: Key-value parameters passed to the run, for example {environment: "prod"}. Keys must match parameters declared on the job.

properties.label: Idempotency token
properties.description: Note: without a token, a connector retry can start the job a second time. Databricks accepts at most 64 characters.

pattern.message: Databricks accepts at most 64 characters, or use a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: Databricks returns the existing run instead of starting a new one when a token is reused. Deriving it from a process variable makes the trigger safe to retry. The literal-value check cannot see through a FEEL expression, so make sure what it evaluates to also stays within 64 characters -- a process instance key is fine, a concatenation of several ids may not be.

properties.label: Run ID

pattern.message: Must be a non-negative integer, or a FEEL expression

properties.tooltip: The run_id returned by Run job now. Exception: for Get run output on a multi-task job, Databricks only accepts a single task's run_id -- read it from the terminal Get run response's tasks[].run_id, not this top-level run_id.

properties.label: Index name
properties.tooltip: Three-level Unity Catalog name of the vector search index.

properties.label: Query payload
properties.tooltip: Request body for the index query. columns is required, but so is exactly one of query_text or query_vector -- a columns-only payload is rejected with HTTP 400 INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. Use query_text for a Delta Sync index backed by a model endpoint, or query_vector for a Direct Vector Access index or a Delta Sync index with self-managed vectors. Optional fields: num_results, filters_json, query_type, and score_threshold.

properties.tooltip: Extra headers to send with the request. The User-Agent required for Databricks partner attribution is set by this template and cannot be overridden here.

properties.description: GET for read operations, POST for everything else.

properties.description: User-Agent is merged last, with any case-insensitive user-agent key stripped first, so the partner attribution value cannot be overridden by additional headers.
properties.value: =context merge(concatenate((for e in get entries(if additionalHeadersInput = null then {} else additionalHeadersInput) return if lower case(e.key) = "user-agent" then {} else context put({}, e.key, e.value)), [{"User-Agent": "Camunda_DatabricksConnector/1.0"}]))

properties.description: Operation-specific request body. Null optional fields are omitted, GET operations send no body, and for chat stream is merged last so it stays false.
properties.value: =if operationInput = "sql.execute" then context merge([ {statement: sqlStatementTextInput, warehouse_id: sqlWarehouseIdInput, wait_timeout: sqlWaitTimeoutInput, on_wait_timeout: sqlOnWaitTimeoutInput, disposition: sqlDispositionInput, format: "JSON_ARRAY"}, if sqlCatalogInput = null then {} else {catalog: sqlCatalogInput}, if sqlSchemaInput = null then {} else {schema: sqlSchemaInput}, if sqlParametersInput = null then {} else {parameters: sqlParametersInput}]) else if operationInput = "serving.chat" then context merge([ if chatExtraParamsInput = null then {} else chatExtraParamsInput, if chatMaxTokensInput = null then {} else {max_tokens: chatMaxTokensInput}, if chatTemperatureInput = null then {} else {temperature: chatTemperatureInput}, {messages: chatMessagesInput, stream: false}]) else if operationInput = "serving.raw" then servingRawPayloadInput else if operationInput = "jobs.runNow" then context merge([{job_id: jobIdInput}, if jobParametersInput = null then {} else {job_parameters: jobParametersInput}, if idempotencyTokenInput = null then {} else {idempotency_token: idempotencyTokenInput}]) else if operationInput = "jobs.cancelRun" then {run_id: runIdInput} else if operationInput = "vectorSearch.query" then vectorQueryPayloadInput else if list contains(["sql.cancel", "warehouse.start", "warehouse.stop"], operationInput) then {} else null

properties.label: Read timeout in seconds
properties.tooltip: Must exceed the SQL wait timeout. Model Serving allows up to 597 seconds of model execution per request, so raise this for slow inference. Use 0 for an infinite timeout.

properties.label: Result variable
properties.tooltip: Name of the process variable that receives the whole response. See result variable.

properties.label: Result expression
properties.tooltip: Maps the response into process variables, and the shape differs per operation. Execute statement returns status.state plus result.data_array, Run job now returns run_id, Get run returns state.life_cycle_state and state.result_state, and chat returns choices, where FEEL lists are 1-indexed. See result expression.

properties.label: Error expression
properties.description: Note: a failed SQL statement returns HTTP 200 with status.state FAILED, so the status code alone does not indicate success. Branch on the state with a gateway rather than here -- see the README.
properties.tooltip: Left empty on purpose. An error expression sees the mapped output whenever Result variable or Result expression is set, not the raw response, so one written against response.body silently stops firing as soon as a result mapping exists -- which is the normal way to use this task. Map status.state into a variable and branch on it with an exclusive gateway instead. If you do write an expression here, write it against whatever your result mapping produces, and remember it is evaluated on the response alone with no way to tell which operation produced it -- guard on the SQL-specific statement_id so a Model Serving raw payload carrying its own status.state is not misread as a SQL failure. Terminal SQL failure states are FAILED and CANCELED; CLOSED means "execution successful, and statement closed; result no longer available for fetch", and PENDING/RUNNING mean the statement is still executing.

properties.label: Retries
properties.description: Several operations here are non-idempotent writes (Execute statement, Run job now). A retry resends the identical request, which can duplicate a SQL INSERT/UPDATE or launch a duplicate job run. The SQL Statement Execution API has no idempotency key at all; Run job now accepts one (see Idempotency token below), but only if it is set. Defaults to 0 for that reason -- raise it only for read-only operations or once you have confirmed the mitigation covers your case.

properties.label: Retry backoff
properties.tooltip: ISO 8601 duration to wait between retries.

properties.label: Job timeout
properties.description: Must exceed Read timeout in seconds above, or Zeebe can consider the job timed out and reactivate it on another worker while this HTTP request is still in flight -- a duplicate non-idempotent call that Retries = 0 does not prevent, because it happens outside the connector.
properties.tooltip: ISO-8601 duration after which Zeebe considers this job timed out if not yet completed. Leave empty to use the default timeout. Raise this alongside Read timeout in seconds when waiting on slow Model Serving inference (up to 597s) or a long SQL wait_timeout.

properties.label: System prompt
properties.value:
="You are **TaskAgent**, a helpful, generic chat agent that can handle a wide variety of customer requests using your own domain knowledge **and** any tools explicitly provided to you at runtime.

If tools are provided, you should prefer them instead of guessing an answer. You can call the same tool multiple times by providing different input values. Don't guess any tools which were not explicitly configured. If no tool matches the request, try to generate an answer. If you're not able to find a good answer, return with a message stating why you're not able to.

Wrap minimal, inspectable reasoning in *exactly* this XML template:

<thinking>
<context>…briefly state the customer’s need and current state…</context>
<reflection>…list candidate tools, justify which you will call next and why…</reflection>
</thinking>

Reveal **no** additional private reasoning outside these tags."

properties.label: System prompt
properties.value:
="You are **TaskAgent**, a helpful, generic chat agent that can handle a wide variety of customer requests using your own domain knowledge **and** any tools explicitly provided to you at runtime.

If tools are provided, you should prefer them instead of guessing an answer. You can call the same tool multiple times by providing different input values. Don't guess any tools which were not explicitly configured. If no tool matches the request, try to generate an answer. If you're not able to find a good answer, return with a message stating why you're not able to.

Wrap minimal, inspectable reasoning in *exactly* this XML template:

<thinking>
<context>…briefly state the customer’s need and current state…</context>
<reflection>…list candidate tools, justify which you will call next and why…</reflection>
</thinking>

Reveal **no** additional private reasoning outside these tags."

name: Generate Content with Google Gemini
description: A large language model (LLM) created by Google AI. It's a multimodal model, meaning it can understand and work with different types of information like text, code, audio, images, and video

properties.label: System instructions
properties.tooltip: System instructions inform how the model should respond. Use them to give the model context to understand the task, provide more custom responses and adhere to specific guidelines. Instructions apply each time you send a request to the model. Learn more about system instructions

properties.label: Grounding
properties.tooltip: Grounding connects model output to verifiable sources of information. This is useful in situations where accuracy and reliability are important. Learn more about grounding

properties.label: Safety Filter Settings
properties.tooltip: You can adjust the likelihood of receiving a model response that could contain harmful content. Content is blocked based on the probability that it's harmful. See the safety filters and attributes.

properties.label: Hate speech
properties.tooltip: Adjust how much potentially harmful content is blocked, based on the probability that it's harmful: OFF blocks nothing, Block few blocks only high-probability content, Block some blocks medium-and-above, and Block most blocks low-and-above. Learn more about safety filters

properties.label: Dangerous content
properties.tooltip: Adjust how much potentially harmful content is blocked, based on the probability that it's harmful: OFF blocks nothing, Block few blocks only high-probability content, Block some blocks medium-and-above, and Block most blocks low-and-above. Learn more about safety filters

properties.label: Sexually explicit content
properties.tooltip: Adjust how much potentially harmful content is blocked, based on the probability that it's harmful: OFF blocks nothing, Block few blocks only high-probability content, Block some blocks medium-and-above, and Block most blocks low-and-above. Learn more about safety filters

properties.label: Harassment content
properties.tooltip: Adjust how much potentially harmful content is blocked, based on the probability that it's harmful: OFF blocks nothing, Block few blocks only high-probability content, Block some blocks medium-and-above, and Block most blocks low-and-above. Learn more about safety filters

properties.label: Add stop sequence
properties.tooltip: A stop sequence is a series of characters (including spaces) that stops response generation if the model encounters it. The sequence is not included as part of the response. You can add up to five stop sequences.

properties.label: Temperature

pattern.message: value must be in the range from 0 to 2 in increments of 0.1

properties.tooltip:
Temperature controls the randomness in token selection.
A lower temperature is good when you expect a true or correct response. 
A temperature of 0 means the highest probability token is usually selected.
A higher temperature can lead to diverse or unexpected results. Some models have a higher temperature max to encourage more random responses.

properties.label: Output token limit from 1 to 8192

pattern.message: value must be whole numbers that range from -2,147,483,647 to 2,147,483,647

properties.tooltip:
Setting a seed value is useful when you make repeated requests and want the same model response.
Deterministic outcome isn’t guaranteed. Changing the model or other settings can cause variations in the response even when you use the same seed value.

properties.label: Top-K

pattern.message: value must be an integer between 1 and 40

properties.tooltip: Top-K specifies the number of candidate tokens when the model is selecting an output token. Use a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.

properties.label: Top-P

pattern.message: value must be in the range from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1

properties.tooltip: Top-p changes how the model selects tokens for output. Tokens are selected from most probable to least until the sum of their probabilities equals the top-p value. For example, if tokens A, B, and C have a probability of .3, .2, and .1 and the top-p value is .5, then the model will select either A or B as the next token (using temperature). For the least variable results, set top-P to 0.

groups.label: Correlation

groups.label: Deduplication

name: SNS HTTPS Message Start Event Connector Subscription
description: Receive messages from AWS SNS via HTTPS.

properties.label: Subscription ID
properties.tooltip: The subscription ID is a part of the URL endpoint

properties.label: Allow to receive messages from topic(s)

properties.tooltip: Topic ARNs that are allowed to trigger the process, comma-separated

properties.label: Activation condition
properties.description: Condition under which the Connector triggers. Leave empty to catch all events

properties.label: Consume unmatched events
properties.tooltip: Unmatched events are rejected by default, allowing the upstream service to handle the error. Check this box to consume unmatched events and return a success response

properties.label: Subprocess correlation required
properties.description: Indicates whether correlation is required. This is needed for event-based subprocess message start events

properties.label: Correlation key (process)
properties.description: Sets up the correlation key from process variables

properties.description: Extracts the correlation key from the incoming message payload

properties.label: Message ID expression
properties.description: Expression to extract unique identifier of a message

properties.label: Message TTL
properties.description: Time-to-live for the message in the broker (ISO-8601 duration)

properties.label: Message name
properties.tooltip: By default, this is an auto-generated random UUID. We recommend using a unique message name for each connector element in the diagram. Override to set a custom message name. Learn more about message subscriptions that power inbound connectors.

properties.label: Manual mode
properties.description: By default, similar connectors receive the same deduplication ID. Customize by activating manual mode

name: Google Sheets Outbound Connector
description: Manage spreadsheets with Google Sheets

properties.label: Parent folder ID
properties.tooltip: Folder in which the new spreadsheet is created. If left empty, it is created in the Google Drive root folder of the OAuth token owner.

properties.label: Cell ID
properties.tooltip: Target cell in ColumnRow format. See the add values to spreadsheet operation.

properties.label: Dimension
properties.tooltip: What to add: column or row

properties.label: Start index
properties.tooltip: Leave empty to add to the end of the sheet. Count starts from 0. See the create empty column or row operation.

properties.label: End index
properties.tooltip: Leave empty to add to the end of the sheet. Count starts from 0. See the create empty column or row operation.

properties.label: Row index
properties.tooltip: Position of the row, shown to the left of each row. If left empty, a new row is appended to the end. See what is a row index.

properties.label: Enter values
properties.tooltip: List of cell values to add as a new row. See the create row operation.

properties.label: Worksheet index
properties.tooltip: Position of the new worksheet; count starts from 0. Leave empty to add it to the end of the sheet list. See what is a worksheet index.

properties.label: Index format
properties.tooltip: How the column to delete is identified: Numbers (numeric index at the top of the column, starting from 0) or Letters (the column letter). See defining which column will be deleted.

properties.label: Column numeric index
properties.tooltip: Numeric position of the column to delete; count starts from 0 (column A is 0, B is 1). See defining which column will be deleted.

properties.label: Column letter index
properties.tooltip: Letter of the column to delete, as shown at the top of the column. See defining which column will be deleted.

properties.label: Row index
properties.tooltip: Position of the row to retrieve, shown to the left of each row. See what is a row index.

properties.label: Version
properties.description: Version of the element template

properties.label: ID
properties.description: ID of the element template

properties.label: Result variable
properties.description: Name of variable to store the response in. Details in the documentation.

properties.label: Result expression
properties.description: Expression to map the response into process variables. Details in the documentation.

properties.label: Error expression
properties.description: Expression to handle errors. Details in the documentation.

properties.label: Retries
properties.description: Number of retries

properties.label: Retry backoff
properties.description: ISO-8601 duration to wait between retries

properties.label: Job timeout
properties.description: ISO-8601 duration after which Zeebe considers this job timed out if not yet completed. Leave empty to use the default timeout

properties.value: ="You are **TaskAgent**, a helpful, capable agent that can handle a wide variety of customer requests using your own knowledge **and** any tools explicitly provided to you at runtime. Prefer a provided tool over guessing whenever it would give a more accurate or reliable answer, and only use tools that were explicitly configured for you (never assume a tool exists). If no tool fits the request, answer from your own knowledge; if you can't produce a reliable answer, say so plainly and explain why, rather than guessing."

properties.label: System prompt
properties.value: ="You are **TaskAgent**, a helpful, capable agent that can handle a wide variety of customer requests using your own knowledge **and** any tools explicitly provided to you at runtime. Prefer a provided tool over guessing whenever it would give a more accurate or reliable answer, and only use tools that were explicitly configured for you (never assume a tool exists). You can call the same tool multiple times with different inputs if that helps complete the request. If no tool fits the request, answer from your own knowledge; if you can't produce a reliable answer, say so plainly and explain why, rather than guessing."

properties.label: Tool call results

properties.description: Avoid reusing context variables across agents to prevent issues with stale data or tool access.
properties.tooltip: The agent context variable containing all relevant data for the agent to support the feedback loop between user requests, tool calls and LLM responses. Make sure this variable points to the context variable which is returned from the agent response. See documentation for details.

properties.label: Parse text as JSON
properties.description: Tries to parse the LLM response text as JSON object.
properties.tooltip:
Use this option in combination with models which don't support native JSON mode/structured tool calling (e.g. Anthropic). Make sure to instruct the model to return valid JSON in the system prompt. The parsed JSON will be available as response.responseJson.

If parsing fails, null will be returned as JSON response, but the text content will still be available as response.responseText.

properties.tooltip: If supported by the model, the response will be structured according to the provided schema. A parsed version of the response will be available as response.responseJson.

properties.label: Response JSON schema name
properties.description: An optional name for the response JSON Schema to make the model aware of the expected output.

properties.label: Include assistant message
properties.description: Include the full assistant message as part of the result object.
properties.tooltip: In addition to the text content, the assistant message may include multiple additional content blocks and metadata (such as token usage). The message will be available as response.responseMessage.
